barbados-cherry-acerola.foliage: Species-level: evergreen; mature leaves are glossy and dark green.
barbados-cherry-acerola.shape: Species-level: bushy shrub or small tree with erect, spreading or drooping branches.
barbados-cherry-acerola.watering: Species-level: tolerates drought, though rain may precede fruiting.
barbados-cherry-acerola.soil: Species-level: reported on limestone, marl and clay soils.
barbados-cherry-acerola.floweringOrFruiting: Species-level: pink or lavender flowers; fruit may mature about 22 days after flowering.

rambutan-rongrien-grafted.matureHeight: Species-level: cultivated trees commonly 4–7 m; wild trees may be taller.
rambutan-rongrien-grafted.light: Species-level: sunny position; young trees benefit from shelter.
rambutan-rongrien-grafted.watering: Species-level: prefers humid conditions and moist soil; no irrigation schedule verified.
rambutan-rongrien-grafted.soil: Species-level: prefers fertile, moist soil rich in organic matter.
rambutan-rongrien-grafted.floweringOrFruiting: Species-level: produces hairy, juicy fruit; Rongrien-specific traits and timing were not verified.

purple-mangosteen.foliage: Species-level: evergreen, thick, leathery, dark-green leaves.
purple-mangosteen.watering: Species-level: needs humid conditions and regular moisture; prolonged drought is unsuitable.
purple-mangosteen.soil: Species-level: deep, rich organic soil with good drainage.
purple-mangosteen.floweringOrFruiting: Species-level: round, dark-purple fruit with white, juicy segments.

loquat-tanaka-grafted.foliage: Species-level: evergreen; large, thick leaves are glossy above and hairy beneath.
loquat-tanaka-grafted.matureHeight: Species-level: about 6–9 m; cited Tanaka description reports a medium-sized tree near 3 m.
loquat-tanaka-grafted.watering: Species-level: ample irrigation is recommended for good fruit production.
loquat-tanaka-grafted.soil: Species-level: tolerates moderately fertile soils; good drainage is important.
loquat-tanaka-grafted.floweringOrFruiting: Tanaka profile: large orange to orange-yellow fruit with juicy, sweet or subacid flesh; ripening season is regional.

wood-apple-velaga.shape: Species-level: erect tree with outward-bending upper branches and drooping branchlet tips.
wood-apple-velaga.floweringOrFruiting: Species-level: small flowers in loose panicles; fruit has a hard woody rind and brown pulp.

bael-maredu.matureHeight: Species-level: reports range from about 6–8 m to 12–15 m.
bael-maredu.watering: Species-level: drought-tolerant; a specific watering schedule is not stated.
bael-maredu.soil: Species-level: adaptable across soil types and a wide pH range.
bael-maredu.floweringOrFruiting: Species-level: fragrant flowers; fruit develops over about 10–11 months from bloom.

red-water-apple-grafted.foliage: Species-level: opposite, simple leaves, green to bluish-green.
red-water-apple-grafted.floweringOrFruiting: Species-level: fragrant yellowish-white flowers in panicles; typically reddish, pear-shaped fruit with juicy white flesh.

banana-tissue-culture-g9.foliage: Species-level: large leaf blades; leaf sheaths form pseudostems.
banana-tissue-culture-g9.shape: Species-level: herbaceous clump of upright pseudostems.
banana-tissue-culture-g9.light: Species-level: full sun for best production; tolerates some shade.
banana-tissue-culture-g9.watering: Species-level, Florida guidance: about 2.5–3.8 cm weekly; avoid flooding and persistently wet soil.
banana-tissue-culture-g9.floweringOrFruiting: If G9 means Grand Naine, TNAU describes long cylindrical fruit and 10–12 hands per bunch; that identity was not verified for this listing.

banana-tella-chakkerakeli.foliage: Species-level: large leaf blades; leaf sheaths form pseudostems.
banana-tella-chakkerakeli.shape: Species-level: herbaceous clump of upright pseudostems.
banana-tella-chakkerakeli.light: Species-level: full sun for best production; tolerates some shade.
banana-tella-chakkerakeli.watering: Species-level, Florida guidance: about 2.5–3.8 cm weekly; avoid flooding and persistently wet soil.
banana-tella-chakkerakeli.floweringOrFruiting: TNAU describes Chakkerakeli fruit as sweet and juicy; identity with this Tella-named plant is unconfirmed.

banana-red-chakkerakeli.foliage: Species-level: large leaf blades; leaf sheaths form pseudostems.
banana-red-chakkerakeli.shape: Species-level: herbaceous clump of upright pseudostems.
banana-red-chakkerakeli.light: Species-level: full sun for best production; tolerates some shade.
banana-red-chakkerakeli.watering: Species-level, Florida guidance: about 2.5–3.8 cm weekly; avoid flooding and persistently wet soil.
banana-red-chakkerakeli.floweringOrFruiting: Bananas are borne in bunches; Red Dacca-specific fruit and crop details were not verified.

banana-amruthapani.foliage: Species-level: large leaf blades; leaf sheaths form pseudostems.
banana-amruthapani.matureHeight: TNAU's Rasthali profile, identified there as Amruthapani, gives about 4–4.5 m.
banana-amruthapani.shape: Species-level: herbaceous clump of upright pseudostems.
banana-amruthapani.light: Species-level: full sun for best production; tolerates some shade.
banana-amruthapani.watering: Species-level, Florida guidance: about 2.5–3.8 cm weekly; avoid flooding and persistently wet soil.
banana-amruthapani.floweringOrFruiting: TNAU's Rasthali profile describes sweet, aromatic fruit; cultivar identity with this product is not independently confirmed.

banana-karpuravalli.foliage: Species-level: large leaf blades; leaf sheaths form pseudostems.
banana-karpuravalli.shape: TNAU describes Karpuravalli as stout and vigorous.
banana-karpuravalli.light: Species-level: full sun for best production; tolerates some shade.
banana-karpuravalli.watering: Species-level, Florida guidance: about 2.5–3.8 cm weekly; avoid flooding and persistently wet soil.
banana-karpuravalli.soil: TNAU describes the cultivar as suited to medium-rich soils and able to thrive in alkaline soils.
banana-karpuravalli.floweringOrFruiting: TNAU describes sweet, juicy fruit; reported crop duration is about 12–14 months in its regional guidance.

banana-curry-cooking.foliage: Species-level: large leaf blades; leaf sheaths form pseudostems.
banana-curry-cooking.shape: Species-level: herbaceous clump of upright pseudostems.
banana-curry-cooking.light: Species-level: full sun for best production; tolerates some shade.
banana-curry-cooking.watering: Species-level, Florida guidance: about 2.5–3.8 cm weekly; avoid flooding and persistently wet soil.
banana-curry-cooking.floweringOrFruiting: If this listing refers to Monthan, TNAU describes a cooking banana with firm, cream-coloured pulp; identity was not independently verified.

papaya-red-lady.foliage: Species-level: palmately lobed leaves, typically on a single trunk.
papaya-red-lady.shape: Species-level: upright, usually single-trunked; secondary shoots may form.
papaya-red-lady.watering: Species-level: regular moisture is important; frequency depends on soil and weather.
papaya-red-lady.soil: Species-level: well-drained soils, including sands, loams and rocky soils.
papaya-red-lady.floweringOrFruiting: Species-level: under good care, flowering may begin about 4 months after planting and fruiting around 7–11 months; Red Lady-specific timing was not verified.

nuda-ficus-multi-step.foliage: Evergreen, glossy leaves; ‘Nuda’-specific traits are not established.
nuda-ficus-multi-step.matureHeight: Ficus benjamina can reach about 12–15 m; the trained topiary size depends on pruning.
nuda-ficus-multi-step.shape: Trained multi-tier topiary, not the species’ natural form.
nuda-ficus-multi-step.watering: Water before the potting mix dries out completely.
nuda-ficus-multi-step.floweringOrFruiting: May produce small fig-like fruits; fruiting is not assured.

nuda-ficus-multi-ball.foliage: Evergreen, glossy leaves; ‘Nuda’-specific traits are not established.
nuda-ficus-multi-ball.matureHeight: Ficus benjamina can reach about 12–15 m; the trained topiary size depends on pruning.
nuda-ficus-multi-ball.shape: Trained multi-ball topiary, not the species’ natural form.
nuda-ficus-multi-ball.watering: Water before the potting mix dries out completely.
nuda-ficus-multi-ball.floweringOrFruiting: May produce small fig-like fruits; fruiting is not assured.

micro-ficus-cone-shape.matureHeight: Ficus microcarpa can reach about 12 m; the clipped cone size depends on pruning.
micro-ficus-cone-shape.shape: Clipped cone topiary, distinct from the species’ natural crown.
micro-ficus-cone-shape.light: Bright light to full sun; protect from cold.
micro-ficus-cone-shape.watering: Water thoroughly when the soil is slightly dry.
micro-ficus-cone-shape.soil: Well-drained soil; a free-draining bonsai mix suits container-grown plants.
micro-ficus-cone-shape.floweringOrFruiting: May produce small fig-like fruits; pollination and fruiting are not assured.

conocarpus-erectus.lifespan: Long-lived landscape tree; no reliable numeric lifespan stated.
conocarpus-erectus.matureHeight: About 9–14 m; open-grown specimens may be smaller.
conocarpus-erectus.shape: Naturally vase-shaped to spreading, often multi-trunked; tolerates clipping.
conocarpus-erectus.watering: Water while establishing; established plants have high drought tolerance.
conocarpus-erectus.soil: Tolerates varied soils, including sand, clay, wet, and well-drained sites.
conocarpus-erectus.floweringOrFruiting: Small green flowers in heads; hard, round reddish-brown fruits can occur year-round.

ficus-bonsai-aged.foliage: Evergreen; leaf size and form vary among Ficus varieties.
ficus-bonsai-aged.matureHeight: Ficus microcarpa can reach about 12 m; bonsai height is determined by training.
ficus-bonsai-aged.shape: Aged bonsai styling is trained and does not indicate the species’ natural shape or lifespan.
ficus-bonsai-aged.light: Abundant light, preferably full sun; protect from frost.
ficus-bonsai-aged.watering: Water thoroughly when the soil is slightly dry.
ficus-bonsai-aged.floweringOrFruiting: May produce small fig-like fruits; fruiting is not assured.

ficus-microcarpa-root-bonsai.matureHeight: Ficus microcarpa can reach about 12 m; bonsai height is determined by training.
ficus-microcarpa-root-bonsai.shape: Aerial-root display is a trained bonsai feature; aerial roots can develop in humid conditions.
ficus-microcarpa-root-bonsai.light: Abundant light, preferably full sun; protect from frost.
ficus-microcarpa-root-bonsai.watering: Water thoroughly when the soil is slightly dry.
ficus-microcarpa-root-bonsai.floweringOrFruiting: May produce small fig-like fruits; fruiting is not assured.

ficus-microcarpa-cloud-bonsai-xl.matureHeight: Ficus microcarpa can reach about 12 m; the cloud-trained form is maintained by pruning.
ficus-microcarpa-cloud-bonsai-xl.shape: Cloud-trained bonsai; the tiered silhouette is not the species’ natural crown.
ficus-microcarpa-cloud-bonsai-xl.light: Abundant light, preferably full sun; protect from frost.
ficus-microcarpa-cloud-bonsai-xl.watering: Water thoroughly when the soil is slightly dry.
ficus-microcarpa-cloud-bonsai-xl.floweringOrFruiting: May produce small fig-like fruits; fruiting is not assured.

ficus-microcarpa-ball-head.matureHeight: Ficus microcarpa can reach about 12 m; trained specimen dimensions depend on pruning.
ficus-microcarpa-ball-head.shape: Ball-head trained specimen; the clipped form is not the natural crown.
ficus-microcarpa-ball-head.light: Abundant light, preferably full sun; protect from frost.
ficus-microcarpa-ball-head.watering: Water thoroughly when the soil is slightly dry.
ficus-microcarpa-ball-head.soil: Free-draining bonsai mix or well-drained soil.
ficus-microcarpa-ball-head.floweringOrFruiting: May produce small fig-like fruits; fruiting is not assured.

ficus-round-ball-shaped.matureHeight: Ficus benjamina can reach about 12–15 m; the trained ball size depends on pruning.
ficus-round-ball-shaped.shape: Rounded ball topiary; the species naturally has drooping branches.
ficus-round-ball-shaped.watering: Water before the potting mix dries out completely.
ficus-round-ball-shaped.floweringOrFruiting: May produce small fig-like fruits; fruiting is not assured.

ficus-umbrella-shape.shape: Umbrella-trained silhouette; the species and natural mature form are unspecified.
ficus-umbrella-shape.light: General Ficus bonsai guidance favors abundant light; protect from frost.
ficus-umbrella-shape.watering: For bonsai, water thoroughly when the soil is slightly dry.
ficus-umbrella-shape.floweringOrFruiting: Ficus species may produce fig-like fruits; species-specific details are unknown.

banyan-specimen.matureHeight: Can reach about 30 m, with a very broad crown and descending aerial roots.
banyan-specimen.shape: Large spreading tree; aerial roots can form additional trunks.
banyan-specimen.floweringOrFruiting: Flowers are enclosed in figs; small fruits may form.

bougainvillea-bonsai.foliage: Foliage varies among Bougainvillea species and cultivars.
bougainvillea-bonsai.shape: Woody scrambling vine; can be trained as a container shrub or bonsai.
bougainvillea-bonsai.watering: Drought-tolerant once established; avoid waterlogged soil.
bougainvillea-bonsai.floweringOrFruiting: Small tubular flowers are surrounded by showy bracts; flowers form on new growth.

tamarind-bonsai.lifespan: Species can live for centuries; UF/IFAS reports up to about 200 years, not a bonsai lifespan guarantee.
tamarind-bonsai.matureHeight: Species can reach about 24–30 m; bonsai size depends on training.
tamarind-bonsai.shape: Naturally stout-trunked with a spreading canopy; bonsai form is trained.
tamarind-bonsai.floweringOrFruiting: Produces brown pods; fruiting is not assured in bonsai.

premna-bonsai.foliage: Often evergreen with small opposite leaves.
premna-bonsai.shape: Trained bonsai; Premna species are trees or shrubs with fine branching.
premna-bonsai.light: Sunny, airy position; protect small specimens from intense midday sun.
premna-bonsai.watering: Keep slightly moist; do not let the bonsai dry out completely.
premna-bonsai.growthRate: Strong growth is reported for Premna bonsai; species-specific rate is not established.
premna-bonsai.floweringOrFruiting: Small pale flowers may be followed by small dark fruits.

adenium-caudex-specimen.lifespan: Perennial succulent; no reliable numeric lifespan stated.
adenium-caudex-specimen.foliage: Glossy, leathery leaves clustered at branch tips.
adenium-caudex-specimen.shape: Small tree-like succulent with a swollen caudex.
adenium-caudex-specimen.watering: Allow soil to dry between waterings; reduce watering during dormancy.
adenium-caudex-specimen.floweringOrFruiting: Summer flowers may be pink, red, or white; slender pods can form and split when mature.

tulasi-holy-basil.lifespan: Annual or short-lived perennial, depending on climate.
tulasi-holy-basil.foliage: Aromatic, opposite leaves; color varies by plant.
tulasi-holy-basil.soil: Moist, well-drained soil; tolerates varied soil types.
tulasi-holy-basil.floweringOrFruiting: Small flowers grow on spikes; color can vary.

aloe-vera.foliage: Fleshy, toothed leaves in a basal rosette.
aloe-vera.watering: Let soil dry completely between waterings.
aloe-vera.floweringOrFruiting: Mature plants may produce upright stems of tubular yellow-orange flowers.

ashwagandha.lifespan: Perennial in warm climates; often grown as an annual in cooler climates.
ashwagandha.foliage: Simple, gray-green leaves with fine hairs.
ashwagandha.shape: Compact, branching herb or small shrub.
ashwagandha.watering: Water sparingly; allow soil to dry between waterings.
ashwagandha.floweringOrFruiting: Small greenish flowers are followed by red berries enclosed by the calyx.

brahmi.foliage: Small, succulent evergreen leaves on creeping stems.
brahmi.watering: Keep consistently wet; tolerates shallow water.
brahmi.floweringOrFruiting: Small white flowers; flowering can continue over a long season.

lemon-grass.lifespan: Perennial in frost-free climates; often grown as an annual where winters are cold.
lemon-grass.watering: Water regularly during active growth; ensure good drainage.

stevia.lifespan: Tender perennial; often grown as an annual in colder climates.
stevia.foliage: Opposite, slightly toothed leaves on slender stems.
stevia.shape: Upright, branching herb with relatively weak stems.
stevia.watering: Keep evenly moist but well drained.
stevia.floweringOrFruiting: Small white flowers; produces one-seeded fruits.

moringa-drumstick.lifespan: Perennial tree; may be deciduous in dry or cool conditions.
moringa-drumstick.foliage: Feathery, compound leaves with many small leaflets.
moringa-drumstick.matureHeight: Typically about 10–12 m; pruning and conditions affect size.
moringa-drumstick.watering: Water while establishing; needs well-drained soil.
moringa-drumstick.soil: Well-drained soil; tolerates relatively poor soils.
moringa-drumstick.floweringOrFruiting: Pale flowers followed by long, narrow seed pods.

buddha-belly-bamboo.lifespan: Perennial clumping bamboo; culms are shorter-lived than the clump.
buddha-belly-bamboo.foliage: Evergreen, narrow green leaves; culms can develop swollen internodes.
buddha-belly-bamboo.matureHeight: Species may reach about 8–15 m in warm climates; containers stay smaller.
buddha-belly-bamboo.growthRate: Moderate to fast in favorable conditions.
buddha-belly-bamboo.floweringOrFruiting: Flowering is episodic; no reliable species-specific interval stated.

golden-bamboo.lifespan: Perennial clumping bamboo; culms are shorter-lived than the clump.
golden-bamboo.foliage: Evergreen foliage; ‘Vittata’ is grown for yellow culms striped green.
golden-bamboo.matureHeight: Bambusa vulgaris can produce culms about 10–20 m tall in warm climates.
golden-bamboo.shape: Large, upright clump; allow room for mature growth.
golden-bamboo.watering: Water during establishment and dry periods; avoid waterlogging.
golden-bamboo.floweringOrFruiting: Flowering is episodic; selection-specific intervals are not established.

timor-black-bamboo.lifespan: Perennial clumping bamboo; culms are shorter-lived than the clump.
timor-black-bamboo.foliage: Evergreen green leaves; mature culms become dark-colored.
timor-black-bamboo.shape: Clumping bamboo; size depends on climate and growing conditions.
timor-black-bamboo.watering: Water during establishment and dry periods; avoid prolonged waterlogging.
timor-black-bamboo.floweringOrFruiting: Flowering is episodic; species-specific intervals are not established.

green-screening-bamboo.matureHeight: Up to about 7.6 m; cultivar and site affect size.
green-screening-bamboo.shape: Dense, arching clump; often grown as a screen or hedge.
green-screening-bamboo.watering: Water well during the first growing season; prefers moist soil.
green-screening-bamboo.soil: Moist, fertile soil with good drainage.

fountain-grass.lifespan: Perennial in warm climates; often grown as an annual in colder regions.
fountain-grass.foliage: Narrow, arching leaves; color varies by cultivar.
fountain-grass.watering: Drought-tolerant once established; water during establishment and extended dry spells.
fountain-grass.soil: Tolerates a range of soils; good drainage is beneficial.
fountain-grass.floweringOrFruiting: Flower plumes appear from summer until frost.

umbrella-grass.foliage: Green leaf-like bracts radiate from the tops of upright stems.
umbrella-grass.matureHeight: Typically about 1.2 m; can reach about 1.8 m in warm, moist conditions.
umbrella-grass.shape: Upright, clump-forming sedge; stems may flop and root where they touch soil.
umbrella-grass.watering: Keep roots continuously wet or grow in standing water.
umbrella-grass.floweringOrFruiting: Produces an inflorescence; notable fruiting details are not established.

NC State Extension — Tripidium ravennae (Ravenna grass)

euphorbia-cactus-assorted.foliage: Varies by species; some forms have fleshy stems.
euphorbia-cactus-assorted.shape: Varies by species; Euphorbia are not cacti, though some resemble them.
euphorbia-cactus-assorted.floweringOrFruiting: Varies by species; Euphorbia flowers are small cyathia.

agave-americana.lifespan: Long-lived perennial rosette; the flowering rosette dies after blooming, while offsets may persist.
agave-americana.foliage: Large, thick, spiny leaves in a basal rosette.
agave-americana.matureHeight: Up to about 3 m; flowering stalks can reach 5–9 m.
agave-americana.floweringOrFruiting: Greenish-yellow flowers grow on a tall stalk; the flowering rosette dies afterward.

yucca.foliage: Leathery, spineless green to blue-green leaves with soft tips.
yucca.matureHeight: About 4.5–9 m outdoors; smaller as a houseplant.
yucca.shape: Upright shrub or small tree with leaves in rosettes.
yucca.floweringOrFruiting: Creamy-white bell-shaped flowers appear on tall stalks; fleshy brown fruit may follow.

sansevieria-cylindrica.lifespan: Perennial; numeric longevity is not established.
sansevieria-cylindrica.foliage: Upright, cylindrical succulent leaves with longitudinal markings.
sansevieria-cylindrica.matureHeight: Leaves can reach about 2 m; indoor size varies.
sansevieria-cylindrica.shape: Rosette-forming plant with upright cylindrical leaves.
sansevieria-cylindrica.light: Bright indoor light; outdoors, morning sun is suitable.
sansevieria-cylindrica.watering: Water sparingly; allow soil to dry and avoid excess water.
sansevieria-cylindrica.soil: Well-drained potting mix; cactus mix is suitable.
sansevieria-cylindrica.floweringOrFruiting: May flower occasionally in a container.

opuntia-ornamental.foliage: Flattened green to bluish-gray stem pads with areoles; may have spines and fine glochids.
opuntia-ornamental.watering: Drought-tolerant; allow soil to dry between waterings.
opuntia-ornamental.soil: Well-drained sandy or loamy soil; use cactus mix in containers.
opuntia-ornamental.floweringOrFruiting: Opuntia species may flower in late spring or early summer and produce fleshy fruits.

golden-barrel-cactus.foliage: Leafless cactus stem with ribs and long spines.
golden-barrel-cactus.shape: Rounded, barrel-shaped; may elongate with age.
golden-barrel-cactus.watering: Let soil dry between waterings; overwatering risks root rot.
golden-barrel-cactus.soil: Fast-draining cactus mix with coarse sand or perlite.
